sympy__sympy-21930::test_NO.why: The failing assertion wants standalone Bd(i) printed as '{b^\dagger_{i}}'. The ticket asks only that the powered form become "{b^\dagger_{0}}^{2}". Bracing inside the operator's own latex and bracing only under Pow both produce that output, and the ticket does not pick one.

sympy__sympy-21930::test_Tensors.why: The test also requires AntiSymmetricTensor to print as '{t^{ab}_{ij}}'. The ticket never mentions tensors, only "double superscripts containing the dagger command". The Bd assertion in this test has the same ambiguity as test_NO.

sympy__sympy-21930::test_commutation.why: This is the same failing assertion as test_NO: unpowered Bd(i) wrapped in braces. The ticket's example "{b^\dagger_{0}}^{2}" is a Pow case, so bracing at the Pow level is an equally valid reading.

sympy__sympy-21930::test_create.why: The test asserts latex(Bd(i)) == '{b^\dagger_{i}}' with no exponent. The ticket only says the double superscript "should be correct by adding curly brackets", which does not fix where the braces go.

sympy__sympy-21930::test_create_f.why: This is the same Bd(i) brace assertion; the test also expects bare Fd(p) to print as '{a^\dagger_{p}}'. The ticket does not say whether an unpowered operator gets braces.

sympy__sympy-22456::test_String.why: The ticket says String should support "expr.func(*expr.args) == expr", and the failing assertion is exactly st.func(*st.args) == st.

sympy__sympy-23950::test_as_set.why: The ticket says returning Contains is wrong because "Contains is not a set", and its Piecewise example needs as_set() to return a set with as_relational. For Contains(x, S) that set is S. The submission raised NotImplementedError, which leaves the reported Piecewise failure in place. The FiniteSet(y) case with a second free symbol is not addressed in the ticket, but returning the set argument covers it.
